newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Banerj prequalification model published.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Banerj prequalification model published.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state has published the rules under which investors can prequalify for the privatization auction of state bank Banerj, the state planning secretary said.

Marco Aurelio Alencar said Banerj, which was placed under the private management of investment bank Bozano, Simonsen in January with the aim to clean up its books ahead of a sell-off, would be auctioned in December. He said the tender document was due to be published in November.

Under the prequalification model, only investors with capital of at least 200 million reais ($200 million) can participate in the privatization auction. They will have to specify how they are raising the funds for the acquisition of Banerj.
Pension funds will not be allowed to acquire a controlling stake in the privatized bank, but foreign investors are welcome.
Alencar said foreign investors would help to increase competition and raise the sale price of Banerj.
Interested investors will have to apply with the necessary documentation to the Central Bank by October 15 and the approvals will be announced November 4.

Investors will also have to prequalify with Susep, the private institution responsible for supervising Brazil's insurance firms, given that Banerj holds 100 percent of the voting capital in insurance subsidiary Banerj Seguros.
Brazil's National Monetary Council (CMN), the government's most senior monetary policy body, approved the sell-off plan for Banerj last week.
Under the plan, brokerage arm Banerj Distribuidora de Titulos e Valores Mobiliarios will receive a capital injection and be transformed into a bank which will be sold.
"It's a way of purging the bank of those elements which make its recovery unviable, as for example the institutional liabilities with the Central Bank and the federal government," Alencar said.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
